scope: Dense scientific figure study: system, representation, exact operation, worked instance and evidence. Includes the two user-nominated 2026 complexity benchmarks.
counting_policy: One underlying primary paper/report per version-stripped arXiv ID or canonical primary URL. Each numbered/descriptive figure once; subpanels are not extra anchors. One primary corporate family per paper; collaborating institutions retained. Year is first submission/publication, separate from inspected revision.
evidence_policy: Every counted new anchor was rendered and visually inspected; abstracts and metadata alone do not count.
Exact PDF version, SHA-256, page and crop are recorded for reproducibility.
Raw PDF colors and opacity, enclosing group alpha, raster samples, visual observations and recommendations remain distinct.
Raster, outlined, or unidentified Type3 lettering does not establish an exact font family.
Source microtype and routing ambiguities are cautions, not standards to copy.
Invalid glyph mappings are retained as raw values with replacement text; no mathematical symbol is guessed.
artifact_policy: Source PDFs, copyrighted figures and local preview images are research intermediates, not redistributed in this skill. Portable basenames identify them; reproduce inspection from the versioned URL/hash/page/crop. Original new demonstration source is bundled separately.

synthesis.name: Global policy + search topology + expanded local step
synthesis.recipe: Use three horizontal scales: a governing budget/policy strip, a compact search or orchestration topology, and one expanded step with concrete input/output artifacts. Reuse a small state motif between the overview and the local mechanism. Reserve separate corridors for feedback, candidate selection, and evidence flow.
synthesis.why_sophisticated: It explains the system at three semantic resolutions without duplicating the full interior at every node.
cautions: Every branch and queue token must correspond to actual algorithm state.
Enlarge the local detail rather than copying 3–5pt native source labels.
Distinguish predicted evaluation from actual measured validation.

synthesis.name: Parallel perception + validated action storyboard
synthesis.recipe: Start from one fixed scene. Split perception into distinct lanes and expose their intermediate representation. Merge through a small conflict-resolution inset, then show proposed action, validator, and observed state as aligned columns. Include one rejected or stopping action and a ledger of what actually executed.
synthesis.why_sophisticated: It couples multimodal input, abstract decisions, and concrete execution evidence.
cautions: Screenshots should use purposeful crop/zoom, not become unreadable wallpaper.
A proposed action is not an executed action.
Document screenshot overlays and retain consistent source-scene coordinates.

synthesis.name: Intervention + worked example + quantitative evidence
synthesis.recipe: Use a clearly labeled intervention region, a matched before/after or counterfactual example, and a separate evidence region. Hold unaffected fields in fixed positions. Couple curves with a compact illustrative transcript tier only when each adds different information.
synthesis.why_sophisticated: It communicates mechanism, observable consequence, and empirical support together while preserving their different evidentiary status.
cautions: Label fictional/synthetic examples and transcript selection rules.
Do not turn temporal correspondence into a causal claim.
Do not mingle illustrative numbers with measured results.

synthesis.name: Representation lineage + typed evidence lanes
synthesis.recipe: Show the actual representation at each consequential stage: schema snippet, token/queue array, command, table, trace, or plot. Put actions on a slim route and attach the evidence they generate below it. Keep different representations visually distinct; highlight changed fields or decisive fragments.
synthesis.why_sophisticated: The figure explains transformations and provenance, so miniature detail has a scientific job instead of serving as decoration.
cautions: Every code/table fragment must be semantically valid.
A tiny chart can identify an output class but cannot support an unreadable numeric claim.
Use one consistent icon family even when source papers mix metaphors.

screened_but_excluded.title: BrowseComp
screened_but_excluded.reason: Verified candidate but excluded from final 14 because its figures added less sophisticated composition coverage than the2026 contrastive-belief paper.

synthesis.name: Mechanism, closeup, and exact relation matrix
synthesis.structure: Use a small whole-system locator, a large component closeup, and one exact relation view such as an attention mask, dependency table, or state-transition matrix.
construction: Choose one short, concrete sequence or artifact and preserve its labels throughout.
Number the two or three operations that deserve closeups.
Repeat the same tokens on matrix axes.
Use one connector style for execution and another for explanatory zoom.
Size the matrix so its headers remain readable at final print size.
synthesis.information_test: A reader should be able to trace one object from the overview through the closeup and verify one permitted or blocked relation in the matrix.
cautions: A closeup must expose a mechanism; it cannot be another enlarged generic box.
Do not copy the source sub-5-point type or excessive accent count.

synthesis.name: Fixed schema with changing conditioning or training state
synthesis.structure: Show one canonical multimodal object sequence, then vertically aligned variants with the same slots, camera views, token groups, or state fields.
construction: Keep column positions and widths identical.
Use quiet background bands for supplied versus predicted content.
Use a redundant mark such as noise texture, a mask badge, or an outline for the changed state.
Put objective formulas and sample weights above each row.
Use a shared column header if repeated labels would become tiny.
synthesis.information_test: A reader should see the single changed boundary or state without re-reading every object label.
cautions: Do not imply that a learned latent slot is literally a photograph of its semantic quantity.
Do not reorder the schema to make individual rows fit.

synthesis.name: Physical mechanism grounded by matched evidence
synthesis.structure: Pair a compact mechanism with a larger grid of matched scene evidence; repeat one scene or frame-pair throughout the explanation.
construction: Define the comparison unit: same frame, same ROI, same time pair, or same camera view.
Keep that unit aligned across modalities or methods.
Place masks, intervals, or action objects next to the visual evidence they describe.
Give results and failure regions enough area for inspection.
Add timestamps, numeric mask keys, or explicit generated/observed labels.
synthesis.information_test: A reader should identify what was held constant, what changed, and where the claimed effect is visible.
cautions: A photographic mosaic alone does not establish generalization.
Avoid unlabeled diagonal before/after crops when exact spatial comparison matters.

synthesis.name: Systems comparison with an implementation ledger
synthesis.structure: Combine a before/after computational topology with an aligned ledger of tensor dimensions, communication counts, resource use, or uncertainty-bearing performance.
construction: Preserve the same input/output ordering across variants.
Expose the repeated operation that is removed, shared, or moved.
Keep numerical details in a dedicated aligned panel rather than scattering tuples over every edge.
Reserve route corridors before placing dense containers.
Show cost and performance uncertainty where both vary.
synthesis.information_test: A reader should be able to count the relevant operations and connect the structural change to a stated resource or performance consequence.
cautions: Do not claim a causal resource improvement from an unlabeled topology alone.
Keep differing axis ranges and aggregation scopes explicit.

synthesis.title: One mechanism at three scales
synthesis.why: A sophisticated figure exposes different levels of explanation instead of merely increasing box count. The strongest examples connect the system overview to the representation geometry and to the exact operation.
recipe: Allocate the largest stable region to an overview with one readable main path. Use the remaining area for one representation panel and one operator panel. These regions need not have equal width or height.
Carry a small set of semantic object identities across all panels: e.g. query tokens, reference tokens and retained memory. Make the corresponding labels identical.
Let each panel use the right visual form: architecture lanes, token/time strips, tensor cuboids, attention matrices or loss-alignment rows.
Attach explicit dimensions, access-mask axes or transformation examples where they settle a technical ambiguity.
Use saturated color for the novel selection or changed state; keep containers and established operations quieter.
production_rules: Recommended target: 7.5–9 pt ordinary labels at final placement, larger panel headings and a separately readable caption. These are new design recommendations, not claimed source measurements.
Start at final physical width, then choose the number of panels and examples. If an operator becomes unreadable, split it into a second figure or a larger inset.
Use editable vector text, paths and matrices; use raster only for meaningful media evidence.
review_questions: Can the reader find the new computation within five seconds?
Does every detail panel answer a question not already answered by the overview?
Do token identity, axes and endpoints agree across panels?

synthesis.title: Stateful time: static condition, current chunk, retained state and output
synthesis.why: Streaming and systems figures become informative when they expose state and timing boundaries. Merely repeating an encoder block hides the dependency that matters.
recipe: Use a shared time coordinate. Put static conditions in a small side region; keep current inputs and outputs in separate aligned lanes.
Draw the chunk boundary or cache boundary and explicitly name retained, padded, evicted and newly computed objects.
Show at least one nontrivial boundary transition. Use indexed tokens or frame groups so the carried state can be traced.
Use a matrix for many device/time or query/context relationships; use a few explicit arrows for the specific return dependency.
If claiming efficiency, pair a schematic schedule with measured latency or memory data and clearly state units, hardware, batch size and concurrency.
production_rules: Do not use schematic cell counts as runtime evidence.
Encode temporal role redundantly through position, labels and a pattern or border style rather than color alone.
Keep cache-return arrows outside dense content, ending at a named state object or port.
review_questions: Are shared weights and shared state distinguishable?
Does the drawing accidentally suggest future access in a causal path?

synthesis.title: Worked structured artifacts with a visible local change
synthesis.why: The missing ingredient in many plain AI diagrams is an actual object being transformed: a proof, program, instruction, token sequence, mask or grounded description. A small truthful example explains more than an ornamental icon.
recipe: Choose one short input artifact with enough context to understand the operation. Show it before the transformation and after it.
Keep unchanged identifiers, order and phrasing identical so the reader can perform a visual diff.
Assign a persistent numbered marker or highlight to the artifact being selected or modified. Use a second explicit state label for accepted, rejected, unresolved or resolved.
If training is involved, show the aligned target/output positions and exactly where the objective applies.
Place a validator or evidence object beside the changed artifact when success depends on a specific check.
production_rules: Use a real or explicitly synthetic worked example; do not fabricate an experiment result.
Excerpt long code and responses. Preserve the changed span plus only the necessary surrounding context.
Avoid full paragraphs below 7.5 pt. An attractive high-resolution preview is not a paper-size proof.
review_questions: Can the reader name the input and output artifact types?
Does the example demonstrate the claimed operation without suggesting unmeasured generality?

synthesis.title: Controlled comparison: invariants aligned, differences localized
synthesis.why: Comparison becomes precise when identical elements look identical and meaningful differences are placed at corresponding coordinates.
recipe: Choose the comparison axis: method variant, injected prior, objective depth or boundary condition. Keep all other relevant conditions visible and fixed.
Align common module baselines, image viewpoints, token indices and panel scales.
Use accent color only around the changed operation or condition. Keep shared stages neutral.
Allow unequal panel width when complexity genuinely differs, while preserving invariant baselines.
For empirical comparisons, label the intervention and reference target and disclose the example-selection rule.
production_rules: Use named mechanisms instead of generic baseline/ours headings when the figure is intended to teach.
Add redundant labels or patterns for before/after rather than relying on red/green alone.
Do not imply superiority by giving one method a larger or more decorated area.
review_questions: What changed, and what was held fixed?
Can the reader find the difference without comparing unrelated visual styles?
Are selected examples being kept distinct from aggregate evidence?

synthesis.title: Mechanism paired with a matching diagnostic
synthesis.why: Architecture alone cannot establish that the mechanism has the intended effect. The most informative figure sets connect a named mechanism to a diagnostic that measures or illustrates that effect.
recipe: Choose the diagnostic from the claim: temporal alignment uses a time-aligned signal, geometry uses matched viewpoints and local regions, sparse computation uses an access mask, and artifact editing uses a before/after diff.
Use the same scenario, object identities or time coordinates between the method explanation and evidence.
Make units, scale, normalization, reference targets and uncertainty explicit where applicable.
Separate descriptive schematic evidence from measured data; label synthetic examples if used.
Include a failure or limiting case when it materially explains the scope.
production_rules: Never use a visually appealing heatmap as evidence without defining its scalar mapping.
For media evidence, preserve crop, viewpoint, frame timing and display settings across methods.
review_questions: What part of the mechanism does this diagnostic test?
Could scale or normalization create the apparent difference?
Does the evidence support the stated scope?
